text: Large Language Models, or LLMs, are computer programs trained on massive amounts of text from books, websites, and articles. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence based on patterns they have learned. When you give one a prompt, such as a question or instruction, it generates a response by stringing together the most likely words. This is called prompt engineering, and the way you phrase your request can greatly affect the quality of the answer. LLMs can write essays, summarize information, or even translate languages. However, they have limits: they sometimes make up facts, lack true understanding, and cannot learn new information unless they are retrained.
